subtitle.text: Designing a self-service enterprise storefront to streamline cloud application discovery, configuration, and procurement.

sections.sectionSubTitle: Designing a self-service enterprise storefront to streamline cloud application discovery, configuration, and procurement.

text.text:
The Challenge

As the lead designer for the platform initiative, my mandate was to transform a disjointed ecosystem of third-party cloud services into a unified, self-service procurement marketplace. The core design challenge lay in complexity abstraction: translating varied vendor pricing models, intricate software licensing terms, and highly technical private-cloud deployment parameters into a standardized, frictionless catalog experience for enterprise IT buyers.

The Solution

I established an unified storefront framework that consolidated service discovery, configuration, and procurement into a single-page application workflow. By designing a dynamic configuration interface that simplified complex deployment variables in real-time, this structure removed the administrative overhead of buying cloud enterprise software, creating a clear, scalable purchasing pathway across diverse vendor applications.

My Role

Lead Product Designer

Platform Focus

B2B Cloud Marketplace, Ecosystem Scalability, Enterprise SaaS

Timeline

6 Months

Environment

Cloud Procurement Storefront

Deconstructing Cloud Procurement Workflows

The initial challenge was designing a storefront when the platform only had a limited number of applications available at launch. A massive, complex search catalog would feel empty, so we focused on a streamlined, high-impact storefront layout that felt complete on day one while remaining architecturally ready to scale. The discovery phase centered on analyzing how different third-party software products were sold, allowing us to map out a highly adaptable configuration template for the product detail pages that could dynamically accommodate completely different vendor pricing models and deployment variables.

Defining Layout Frameworks and Product Scope

The ideation phase focused on translating our discovery insights into a flexible structural wireframe layout that could scale alongside the growing vendor catalog. Because early application counts were low, we designed a dashboard layout that emphasized prominent service categorization and straightforward discovery pathways, avoiding the need for complex, heavy filtering systems on day one. This structural framework allowed the team to cross-validate feature priorities for the initial launch, ensuring we could map out a clean user progression from landing on the storefront directly into configuring specific vendor software.

Establishing a Scalable Grid Framework

To support a frictionless discovery process, we designed a unified, single-page dashboard layout that houses the entire initial marketplace catalog. The interface organizes third-party cloud services into a clear, scannable grid system, categorized by provider type and infrastructure function (such as application services, data analytics, and developer tools). This layout strategy allows IT operators to instantly scan available cloud solutions, pivot between vendor categories, and view high-level pricing indicators in a single interaction loop, minimizing navigational deep-dives and maintaining high operational clarity.

Contextual Product Configuration and Specs

When an operator selects an application, the interface utilizes an inline expansion panel to reveal comprehensive service details without disrupting their place in the main catalog. This layout serves as the flexible configuration template designed to standardize varied software vendor models. By displaying structured pricing tiers, distinct deployment options, and hardware specifications directly within this contextual panel, users can rapidly configure application variables and evaluate infrastructure compatibility without unnecessary context switching.

Dynamic Parameter Configuration and Checkout

The checkout interface utilizes a split-panel layout to guide users through final deployment variables and financial sign-off. As an IT buyer specifies hosting environments, provisioning regions, and storage scale limits, a dynamic order summary module calculates cost adjustments in real time. This interactive feedback loop replaces manual ordering paperwork with instant operational clarity, giving enterprise procurement teams complete visibility into infrastructure costs and configuration states before committing to a deployment.

Cross-Project Governance and UI Standardization

To maintain product cohesion across the broader cloud portfolio, I established a centralized design specification framework that served as the single source of truth for our UI patterns. This initiative included standardizing core interface components, interaction behaviors, and a custom icon library tailored specifically for technical infrastructure metrics. By formalizing these governance guidelines, we enabled cross-functional product teams to scale marketplace features independently while ensuring visual consistency and cutting down redundant front-end design overhead.

Executive Alignment and Strategic Product Storytelling

A defining milestone of this initiative was driving cross-functional alignment between product engineering, product management, and executive leadership to define the platform's long-term roadmap. By collaborating directly with SVPs and Directors, I translated complex cloud infrastructure capabilities into high-fidelity interactive prototypes and strategic narratives for keynotes at CiscoLive!. This experience reinforced the critical role of product design in executive storytelling using tangible, interactive vision models to secure stakeholder buy-in, align distributed engineering squads, and clearly communicate platform value to the broader market.

subtitle.text: Leading the design of an enterprise visualization platform that transforms complex mathematical verification into an intuitive, proactive monitoring experience for data center operators.

sections.sectionSubTitle: Leading the design of an enterprise visualization platform that transforms complex mathematical verification into an intuitive, proactive monitoring experience for data center operators.

text.text:
The Challenge

As the founding product designer, my mandate was to transform a disjointed collection of engineering-led verification features into a cohesive, centralized enterprise platform. The primary challenge lay in data density. Because the backend generated massive streams of algorithmic network data, the interface was prone to severe information noise. I was tasked with defining the product architecture from scratch, designing advanced data filtering workflows and structural layouts that allowed operators to easily navigate system noise and target specific network errors with precision and speed.

The Solution

I established a visualization framework that translates complex network validation logic into an interactive, timeline-driven dashboard. To solve the problem of tracking network health over time, I introduced a patented navigation interface based on time epochs, allowing users to instantly pivot between historical and real-time network states to isolate exactly when an error occurred. By pairing this timeline with custom data visualization components, this solution enables administrators to slice complex datasets effortlessly, accelerating troubleshooting and surfacing clear remediation paths for system anomalies.

My Role

Lead Product Designer

Partners

Cisco IT, Engineering, Product Management, Tech Marketing

Timeline

6 Months

Product

On-Premises Application

The engagement began with collaborative workshops alongside Cisco IT, technical marketing, and product management to map out core user needs and technical constraints. This deep dive into the architecture of Cisco ACI and network objects allowed me to understand how operators interact with the system. Rather than just cataloging user requests, this baseline knowledge allowed me to identify the structural disconnects between isolated network layers and determine the most effective data presentation formats.

Defining Product Scope and Architecture

The ideation phase focused on translating our technical discovery insights into a scalable structural layout and navigation model. I designed structural framework wireframes to map out exactly how operators would pivot between complex network assurance views without losing their operational context. This architectural exploration allowed the team to cross-validate feature priorities for the initial product release and establish a stable site map before moving into high-fidelity design production.

Time-Epoch Navigation

I introduced a patented timeline interface to serve as the primary navigation framework for tracking network state and health over time. The layout provides explicit visual indicators that flag system issues at exact moments, allowing operators to step through historical states and compare health across different intervals. By linking this time-epoch navigation directly to the backend logic, operators can instantly pinpoint the exact moment a configuration divergence occurred to radically accelerate troubleshooting.

Visualizing Network Dynamics

This interface translates dense configuration tables into an interactive relational map of network objects and their active communication pathways. I structured the visual hierarchy specifically to prioritize communication violations and security policy discrepancies over standard operational data. This design provides operators with a direct, scannable mental model to immediately assess threat severity, manage compliance, and verify active network rules.

Natural Language Query Models

To streamline how operators query dense infrastructure data, I designed an interactive search interface based on natural language logic. The interface reduces cognitive load by structuring queries around core operational intents: What, Can, How, and View. This interaction model translates predictive search selections into precise data visualizations, completely eliminating the need for operators to write custom programmatic syntax to uncover asset dependencies.

Advanced Filtering Controls

To prevent information overload within dense network fabrics, I designed a standardized, multi-layered filtering architecture. This framework allows operators to instantly isolate massive datasets by specific technical parameters, helping them pinpoint exact failure points and execute targeted troubleshooting. By establishing this as a consistent design pattern, we ensured that high-density data controls remain intuitive and predictable across all primary dashboards.

High-Fidelity Interface Delivery & Platform Scale

The final phase translated validated user flows into production-ready interface specifications. I established a visual system that standardized component behaviors, high-density data palettes, and interactive states to ensure platform consistency. To bridge the gap between design strategy and execution, I collaborated closely with engineering teams on implementation, providing a clear development roadmap that ensured a seamless, high-quality production release.

Custom Component Library and Specifications

To support the platform’s dense data requirements, I defined a standardized library of specialized UI components and interactive patterns. This involved establishing semantic color systems for critical network status alerts and creating reusable, high-density components like interactive data tables and layout grids. By delivering these structured UI specifications, I provided engineering teams with a predictable framework that maintains visual cohesion and accelerates implementation across the entire application ecosystem.

Marketing and Partner Video Production

For our partner presentations at CiscoLive!, I led the end-to-end production of our high-fidelity video use cases. I was directly responsible for the conceptualization, illustration, and animation phases, ensuring that complex motion graphics clearly communicated the platform's technical value. Working alongside product managers and designers, I aligned these narrative assets with our primary product goals to deliver a highly impactful audience demonstration.

Scale, Execution, and Technical Milestones

This project demonstrated how strategic product design can drive complex enterprise software from inception to a stable production deployment. Navigating tight execution timelines required balancing system-level product requirements with practical engineering constraints. The resulting interface not only delivered an intuitive operational experience for a highly technical user base, but also established defensive design patterns that protect core visualization frameworks as unique intellectual property.

subtitle.text: Redesigning a highly technical data routing ecosystem to unify fragmented developer workflows and scale enterprise network analytics.

sections.sectionSubTitle: Redesigning a highly technical data routing ecosystem to unify fragmented developer workflows and scale enterprise network analytics.

text.text:
The Challenge

The core challenge lay in translating complex network data routing logic into intuitive operator workflows within an aggressive 2.5-month timeline. The application required a complete structural overhaul to align with a unified platform framework.

The Solution

I mapped complex data streams to clear mental models by collaborating closely with Product Management and Engineering. By leveraging the platform’s core design system, this approach successfully balanced deep backend technical constraints with frontend operational efficiency.

My Role

Lead Product Designer

Partners

Engineering, Product Management, Tech Marketing

Timeline

2.5 Months

Resolving Technical Ambiguity

The engagement began by auditing a loosely defined requirement to improve the user interface. By partnering with engineering, technical marketing, and product leadership, I mapped out the existing system functionality to ensure no critical workflows were lost. This upfront collaboration allowed us to modernize the visual language and maintain deep feature parity while dramatically accelerating the interaction performance of the topology map.

Structuring Complex Workflows

Because direct access to enterprise operators was constrained by deployment security, I leveraged Tech Marketing as a primary validation proxy for domain logic. Analyzing core operational use cases and system constraints across the Nexus Dashboard suite, I mapped out a cohesive product framework that translated these technical insights into structural wireframes. Through iterative prototyping and cross-functional engineering feedback, I streamlined the layout hierarchy to ensure administrators could navigate dense data sets with minimal friction.

Architecting the Analytics Dashboard

Recognizing a critical gap in system health observability, I architected a dedicated traffic monitoring ecosystem. This dashboard surfaces real-time traffic statistics, node statuses, and component utilization at a single glance. By transforming passive data points into actionable diagnostic visualizations, this feature proactively mitigates troubleshooting friction for network operators.

Evolving the Network Topology

To unlock deep system visibility, I transformed the legacy static topology map into an interactive canvas. Administrators can now interact directly with individual infrastructure nodes, view real-time status updates, and configure system components right from the canvas. This completely eliminates the need to toggle between separate configuration pages.

Streamlining Setup Flows

The original configuration pages relied strictly on text boxes and dropdown menus, which made setting up the system a tedious process. I redesigned the UI by introducing visual components that simplify complex selections. This shift helps users process information faster, allowing them to navigate through setup steps with fewer errors and higher efficiency.

Standardizing the Interface

I restructured the application pages to fully integrate with the Nexus Dashboard platform ecosystem. By adopting the established design system components, I brought visual and functional consistency to the user interface. This approach improved the usability of each page and established a reusable foundation that supports future platform updates and scaling.

System Governance, Speed, and Scale

Shipping this application on an aggressive release cycle required clear communication and fast alignment across a complex technical domain. Beyond designing individual screens, I focused on building strong workflows with our engineering partners to ensure we maximized our shared component library. Working with distributed global teams, I established interface patterns that resolved pressing usability problems and gave the team a practical framework for future product updates.
